# Draft:Winter Warrior Finland

Winter Warrior Finland is an international winter Obstacle course racing (OCR) event held in Finland. The race combines traditional OCR obstacles with extreme winter conditions, including snow, ice, and cold water. The event has been described as one of the most challenging winter OCR races.
The event was first held in 2018 in Ylläs, Lapland, and has been organised in Tampere since 2025.
History
Winter Warrior Finland was founded by Finnish organisers Maria Christensen and Simo Lahtinen. The concept was inspired by international obstacle course races, including the Tough Guy Competition, known for its extreme conditions.
The first edition took place on 21 April 2018 in the Pallas–Yllästunturi National Park near Ylläs. From 2018 to 2023, the race was held annually in Ylläs, with courses traversing fell terrain and deep snow, including ascents of local fells such as Kesänki.
The 2020 and 2021 editions were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Virtual challenges were held instead, in which participants submitted recorded performances.
In 2025, Winter Warrior Finland moved to Tampere. The first Tampere edition was held on 1 March 2025, utilising urban landmarks as well as the frozen surface of Lake Näsijärvi. The event returned to Tampere in 2026.
Course and obstacles
The race course combines natural and constructed obstacles. During the Ylläs era, the course emphasised long ascents, fell terrain, and running in deep snow. In Tampere, the route incorporates urban waterfronts and ice-covered sections of Lake Näsijärvi.
One of the event’s best-known obstacles is the I Scream Tunnel, an ice-filled tunnel that competitors crawl through. The obstacle has become a distinctive feature of the race and is frequently mentioned by participants.
Traditions
* Flag Bearers: The first competitor from each country to reach the final section of the course carries their national flag to the finish line. If overtaken by another competitor from the same country, the flag is transferred. In 2025, competitors from 19 countries participated as flag bearers.
* Warrior Spirit Award: An award recognising exceptional perseverance, attitude, or sportsmanship, presented independently of race results.
Results
In its early years (2018–2023), the race featured a single main competitive category. From 2025 onwards, separate competitive divisions were introduced.

In 2025, the men’s Full Warrior title was shared following an exceptionally close finish and course modifications caused by ice conditions.
Values and volunteers
Winter Warrior Finland emphasises environmental responsibility, particularly in national park areas. The event is organised with the support of more than one hundred volunteers each year.
